## Your own percentile {#find-your-own-percentile .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted in Task 4: its output includes your **placement**, the share of the `r format(nrow(spec_curve), big.mark = ",")` specifications on the curve with a more negative claim-aligned *r* than yours. For the reproduced specification it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(spec_curve$r_ca < curve_ref$r_ca))`
- The same statistic that places the reference results, computed for **you**
:::

::: {.fs-80}
**In the IDE workspace:** your call of `try_spec()`, rerun in the console or in the chunk `try-one-at-a-time` of `index.qmd`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# the arguments of the specification submitted in Task 4; as it stands,
# the reproduced specification
try_spec()
```

::: notes
Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted, in your IDE workspace or in this cell if you work in the slides. The placement line in its output is the statistic that places the reference results, the share of the eight hundred and sixty-four specifications on the curve that are more negative than yours. For the reproduced specification, my own model, it is sixty-seven per cent, so if you did not submit, that is your number. [run the cell as it stands] A sentence such as "my estimate sits at the Nth percentile of the specification curve" is a publishable way to report a robustness check, provided that you say how the curve was built.
:::
